findings.reason: a node reading §16 literally re-runs a hoist §17 already landed and renames/relocates live code, so the section must be restated against the post-§17 tree.
findings.text: §16 states "section_record_id and section_id_candidates live today in reckon/crew/routing.py … §17 hoists them into reckon/_plan_html.py" and "section_record_id gains an optional enclosing-attributes parameter and moves", but §17 has landed: the identity trio is already at reckon/_plan_html.py:71/87/92, routing only imports them (reckon/crew/routing.py:29), and section_record_id already accepts `enclosing=`; the same section's interface accounting then reads "§17 has landed its two additions", so the section contradicts itself on §17's state

findings.reason: without naming `roadmap.implementable_sections` as the single owner it consumes, the node may mint a fourth outstanding-sections reader, and the public-definition accounting that credits §18 with a "reader" addition is wrong.
findings.text: §16 needs the set of sections still admitting work and names it inconsistently: twice as "§18's reader" / "the hoisted outstanding-sections reader … §18's addition and counted there", once as `roadmap.implementable_sections`; §18 added no reader, only the `is_implementable_section` predicate, and three readers of that question already exist (`roadmap.implementable_sections` at reckon/roadmap.py:107, `doccheck._implementable_section_ids` at reckon/doccheck.py:1018, `_schema.plan_executable_remainder` at reckon/_schema.py:800)

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — one private `_section_digests(plan)` mapping and the recomposed `plan_fingerprint` hide the section-identity, per-section-prose and document-unit digests behind a single public digest, which is smaller than what it hides.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the outstanding-sections owner is `roadmap.implementable_sections` (`reckon/roadmap.py:107`), which §16 consumes but attributes to "§18's reader"; §18 added only the `is_implementable_section` predicate (`reckon/_schema.py:788`), and two list readers already exist beside roadmap's.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — against this week's public_definitions 1480 / cli_options 317 / mcp_views 33 / refusal_families 23: §16 adds exactly one public definition (`strip_tags`), saying why nothing is retired (the identity digest and prose walk keep their names) and reusing the existing plan-review-missing refusal family; §19 adds no public definition and retires nothing.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §16 both consumes machinery §17 already landed (`section_record_id`, `section_id_candidates`, `section_anchor`, the number core in `reckon/_plan_html.py`) and, in the same text, describes that hoist as this section's own pending work, so the plan's account of prior art is stale.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the one added public name, `strip_tags`, is justified as an outward-facing reuse of the module's existing `_TAG_RE` (chosen over a second expression), and §16 argues at length why the coverage predicate is not a wrapper over `read_plan_review` (one record↔one digest versus a set join).
